description: Default AegisTelemetry out-of-the-box issue detection and recommendation rules. Includes the full built-in issue set: AoE/replication, physics, network packet pressure, local density, AI pathfinding, memory pressure, matchmaking/capacity surge, and desync/hit-registration risk. Developers can add/edit rules here without changing Python code.

rules.title: AoE replication overload
rules.impact: High AoE density is increasing replicated object volume and server frame pressure.
recommended_actions: Reduce temporary AoE object replication radius when local density crosses the configured threshold.
Lower update frequency for non-authoritative AoE visuals/debris while preserving authoritative damage resolution.
Pool and reuse short-lived AoE actors instead of spawning/despawning replicated objects at burst rate.
investigation_steps: Profile the top ability in the affected window with replication and actor-spawn markers enabled.
Compare replicated object count before and after AoE burst windows.
Inspect whether cosmetic AoE components are being replicated to clients that do not need them.
validation_plan: Run a high-density combat simulation with the replication radius change enabled.
Compare p95/p99 server frame time and packet-out rate before/after.
Confirm combat readability and hit registration remain stable.
tradeoffs: Reducing replication radius can improve performance but may reduce visual consistency for distant observers.
Lowering update frequency can reduce bandwidth but may make cosmetic effects appear less smooth.

rules.title: Physics simulation spike
rules.impact: Physics-heavy events are correlated with CPU and server-frame spikes.
recommended_actions: Cap non-critical rigid-body simulation in high-density combat windows.
Convert cosmetic debris to client-side or non-replicated simulation where gameplay correctness does not depend on it.
Batch or throttle physics wake-up events caused by explosions or chained impacts.
investigation_steps: Profile physics step time during affected windows.
Identify the top gameplay event creating physics bodies or wake-ups.
Check whether replicated physics actors can be replaced with deterministic client-side visuals.
validation_plan: Replay the same combat burst with capped physics body counts.
Compare physics step time, CPU p95, and p99 server frame time.
Verify collision/gameplay-critical interactions still behave correctly.
tradeoffs: Physics caps can improve stability but may reduce visual richness in chaotic scenes.

rules.title: Network packet pressure
rules.impact: Packet loss and packet-out pressure are likely contributing to rubberbanding/desync.
recommended_actions: Reduce replication priority for cosmetic and short-lived objects in the affected zone.
Audit high-frequency replicated properties and move non-critical states to lower update cadence.
Enable density-aware relevance filtering for actors outside immediate combat relevance.
investigation_steps: Inspect packet-out rate by server and zone during incident windows.
Break down bandwidth by actor class or replication group.
Compare packet loss against replicated object count and rubberband/desync events.
validation_plan: Run a controlled replication-priority test on the same density scenario.
Compare packet_out_kbps_p95, packet_loss_p95, and correction/rubberband events.
Verify players still receive all combat-critical state updates.
tradeoffs: Aggressive relevance filtering can improve bandwidth but may hide non-critical events too early.

rules.title: Local density tick-budget pressure
rules.impact: Crowding is driving local simulation pressure even without a single dominant event type.
recommended_actions: Introduce density-aware simulation budgets for non-critical systems in crowded zones.
Split encounter objectives or rewards across nearby spaces to reduce forced player stacking.
Evaluate shard/instance splitting if density remains high after design-level spacing changes.
investigation_steps: Compare server frame time against local player density after controlling for AoE, physics, and packet pressure.
Inspect top zones that repeatedly exceed local density thresholds.
Review encounter or reward design that may be forcing players into one zone.
validation_plan: Simulate or stage the encounter with distributed objective placement.
Compare local density, p95 server frame time, and completion/funnel metrics.
Confirm player flow remains understandable and fun.
tradeoffs: Spreading players out can improve performance but may change encounter pacing or social density.

rules.title: AI pathfinding pressure
rules.impact: AI/pathfinding request volume is likely contributing to server-frame spikes.
recommended_actions: Throttle non-critical path recalculations during high-density combat.
Increase path cache reuse for nearby agents with similar goals.
Lower AI update frequency for distant or low-priority agents while preserving combat-critical behavior.
investigation_steps: Inspect pathfinding request volume and active AI count in affected windows.
Profile pathfinding/navmesh query time by AI archetype.
Check whether AoE/physics events are causing excessive AI replanning.
validation_plan: Replay the incident with path recalculation throttling enabled.
Compare AI pathfinding requests, server frame p95/p99, and combat outcome metrics.
Validate AI behavior quality with design/QA review.
tradeoffs: Lower AI update rates can improve server stability but may reduce perceived AI responsiveness.

rules.title: Memory pressure / allocation churn
rules.impact: High memory pressure may be contributing to hitches or unstable server performance.
recommended_actions: Profile allocation churn during incident windows and identify high-volume object creation paths.
Pool frequently spawned gameplay objects and temporary effects.
Audit asset/actor lifetime in the affected zone to reduce memory spikes.
investigation_steps: Collect allocation and GC/profiler markers around the incident window.
Correlate memory p95 with object spawn, replication, and physics events.
Check whether a specific ability or encounter creates long-lived temporary objects.
validation_plan: Run before/after load test with pooling or lifetime reduction enabled.
Compare memory p95, GC time, and p99 server frame time.
Verify gameplay objects are not prematurely destroyed or missing.
tradeoffs: Pooling can improve performance but increases lifecycle complexity and requires strong reset hygiene.

rules.title: Regional capacity / matchmaking surge
rules.impact: Login/session-start pressure indicates the region may need additional capacity.
recommended_actions: Pre-scale regional shards when session-start velocity exceeds baseline.
Temporarily widen matchmaking capacity thresholds if player-experience guardrails remain safe.
Route overflow to adjacent healthy capacity only if latency guardrails are acceptable.
investigation_steps: Compare session-start velocity against historical baseline for the same region/time.
Check shard occupancy, queue length, and session start delay.
Verify whether the surge is tied to a live event, content drop, or outage recovery.
validation_plan: Simulate the next 30 minutes of concurrency using current login velocity.
Compare projected occupancy against target shard utilization.
Confirm queue delay improves after pre-scaling.
tradeoffs: Pre-scaling improves player experience but increases short-term infrastructure cost.

rules.title: Desync / hit-registration risk
rules.impact: Player-impact signals are rising and may degrade combat feel even if server frame time is not the only driver.
recommended_actions: Inspect correction/rubberband and desync events around high-action windows.
Prioritize combat-critical replication over cosmetic or low-priority state updates.
Add targeted telemetry around hit confirmation delay and client correction magnitude.
investigation_steps: Compare desync/rubberband events against packet loss, server frame time, and replicated object count.
Review combat logs for delayed or missing authoritative confirmations.
Check whether specific abilities or zones produce correction spikes.
validation_plan: Run a controlled combat test after prioritizing critical state replication.
Compare desync events, hit confirmation delay, and player correction events.
Use QA/network simulation to test packet loss and latency conditions.
tradeoffs: Prioritizing combat state can reduce bandwidth for cosmetic fidelity under pressure.
